title: Endocrine System: Glands and Hormones
summary: Endocrine glands; anterior and posterior pituitary; thyroid; pancreas; adrenal glands; hormones and their functions.
objectives: Describe the endocrine system and hormone function.
Identify major endocrine glands and key hormones.
revision: Endocrine system = glands secreting hormones into bloodstream. Pituitary = master gland. Anterior pituitary produces tropic hormones; posterior releases ADH and oxytocin.
confusions: Believing all hormones come from the pituitary.

notes.t: A collection of glands that produce hormones — chemical messengers secreted directly into the bloodstream to regulate body processes.

r: Growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, prolactin

notes.t: The pituitary is often called the 'master gland' because it controls other endocrine glands. The anterior pituitary produces several tropic hormones; the posterior pituitary stores and releases ADH and oxytocin.
UGC NET frequently asks about pituitary hormones and endocrine gland functions. ADH = antidiuretic hormone (water balance).

mnemonics.text: G — Growth hormone, T — TSH, A — ACTH, F — FSH, L — LH, P — Prolactin
